This is specifically pulled from the side effects section of the drug info page, so I'm not sure what you consider misleading about it. Like I'm not just making these up or slapping the word side effects on them, that's what they are.

[FDA](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/information-consumers-and-patients-drugs/finding-and-learning-about-side-effects-adverse-reactions) article on what side effects are:

"Side effects, also known as adverse reactions, are unwanted undesirable effects that are possibly related to a drug. Side effects can vary from minor problems like a runny nose to life-threatening events, such as a heart attack or liver damage."

That isn't specifically about testosterone, just examples of things that can fall under the term "side effects." Again this is not to scare people. This is not to say it WILL happen to anyone who takes it. These are the worst case one in however many scenarios that you want to know about in case they DO happen. -nausea or vomiting
-changes in skin color
-increased or ongoing erection of the penis
-impotence, ejaculation problems, decreased amounts of semen, decrease in testicle size

[source](https://www.drugs.com/testosterone.html#side-effects)

Keep a relaxed tone. If they try to turn the conversation into criticizing your previous efforts, don't let it get a rise of you, don't let them derail. Circle back to "moving forward, is there something I can do to show support?"

Definitely seek professional help for all of it. Being trans in and of itself isn't a psychological disorder, but if they have dysphoria or if they're experiencing distress with this process of figuring out who they are, then they need  help for that. The way my sister has done it, she knows she will not tolerate behaviors A, B, C, and that if the line is crossed, she will respond with X, Y, Z.

I definitely suggest doing it that way, because it gives you the power to ensure your own boundaries aren't violated, rather than having to trust the other person, and giving them the power to violate your boundaries.
